text:
Alex: quick sync — we need a concrete proposal for per-org rate smoothing. TPM/RPM + concurrency caps, and how bursts behave. thoughts?
Marta: is the ask mostly about UX (console/quota view) or enforcement semantics?
Alex: both. product wants predictable billing + no noisy tenants killing tail latency. ops want graceful degradation for short spikes.
Sara: TL;DR: implement a two-layer model: long-window quota (RPM/TPM) + short-window burst smoothing (leaky-bucket credits) + concurrency cap. that gives billing predictability and headroom for spikes.
Ian: sounds fine, but need exact numbers & failure modes. what happens when credits exhausted? 429 or queue?
Sara: prefer soft-fail first: return 429 with Retry-After + include X-Quota-Remaining headers, and offer optional queueing for Dedicated customers.
Jordan: +1 for headers. clients need to know remaining tokens for smart backoff. also add telemetry events for throttle_rejected vs throttle_delayed.
Alex: can we show this in console per-route? product wants to show "recent smoothing events" and top offenders.
Marta: UI note: show both short-window (1m) and long-window (1h) usage. also surface last throttle timestamp and percent of quota used.
Ian: enforcement semantics: propose these primitives:
```
policy: {
  rpm: 18000,        # requests per minute (long)
  tpm: 300000,      # tokens per minute (if token accounting)
  burst_capacity: 500, # credits usable in short term
  burst_refill_rate: 8, # credits/sec
  concurrency: 50    # max inflight requests per org
}
```
Alex: we need to be careful with units — some customers meter tokens not requests. must support both.
Sara: agreed. implement a token-agnostic core where burst credits are in "request units" that map to tokens if model-specific.
Jordan: what about fairness across keys in same org? should org-level concurrency be partitioned?
Marta: simplest is org-wide concurrency cap + per-key soft share. i.e., if one key hogs >80% of concurrency, instrument an alert and throttle that key harder.
Ian: ops concern: how to avoid thundering herd when credits refill? e.g., at refill tick many clients retry simultaneously. we should jitter retry-after and add a leaky queue with randomized backoff.
Sara: implement randomized Retry-After in range [base, base*1.2], and emit a spike-mitigation metric when > X retries observed.
Alex: rollout plan? we can't flip org caps on for everyone.
Marta: staged rollout: default policy in console OFF for older orgs, new orgs get defaults ON. provide per-org override toggle + migration tool that previews expected throttles based on past 30d usage.
Jordan: preview is key. product wants an "impact forecast" graph per org (est. throttle minutes, revenue impact).
Ian: telemetry - we need these events: quota_eval, credit_debit, throttle_emit, throttle_queue, throttle_reject. tag with org_id, key_id, route, model, latency_p50/p95.
Sara: add derived metric: throttle_ratio = throttle_reject / requests_total. dashboard tile + alert if > 0.01 for 1h.
Alex: testing: create synthetic tenants with bursty traffic to validate fairness and tail latency. also add integration test for header behavior.
Marta: legal/compliance: any PII in headers? no. but make sure audit logs don't leak prompt contents when storing throttle events.
Jordan: UX detail: headers + response body should contain human-friendly reason codes for developers e.g., {"code":"org_burst_exhausted","retry_after":3}.
Ian: ops: add circuit-breaker fallback to a cheaper model variant when org is throttled and route allows fallback. preserves availability.
Sara: good call. fallback should be opt-in per route in routing policy.
Alex: outstanding decisions: 1) default numerical settings 2) soft vs hard for concurrency cap 3) exact header names 4) console preview UI scope.
Marta: propose defaults (we can tune later): rpm=12000, burst_capacity=300, burst_refill_rate=5/sec, concurrency=30. soft concurrency: allow burst up to 150% for <10s then enforce hard.
Jordan: +1 for soft concurrency. reduces customer surprise.
Ian: note: implement metrics for "short-term burst credit usage" percentile to tune refill rate.
ratebot: deploy scheduled: rate-limiter-service/v2 will add smoothing and headers. canary in us-west-2 next wed. :robot_face:
Alex: thanks team — i'll draft RFC with these primitives and the migration plan, will include sample console mocks and impact forecast outline.
Marta: assign to Alex+Sara for RFC, Ian for infra checklist, Jordan for telemetry & dashboard mocks.
Jordan: I'll add the telemetry schema to the RFC tonight.
Sara: I'll prototype the credit accounting lib and a small sim to tune defaults.
Alex: awesome. meeting notes saved. :thumbsup:
